blocks.content: Plinian eruptions are the most explosive and dangerous type of volcanic eruption, capable of sending ash columns high into the stratosphere.

rows: Gentle lava fountains and broad shield volcano formation
Rhythmic bursts of lava bombs and glowing cinders
Cauliflower-shaped ash clouds resulting from cleared conduit plugs
Colossal stratospheric ash columns and catastrophic pyroclastic flows

items: Silica content and lava viscosity are frequently tested: High silica (felsic) lava causes violent explosions, while low silica (mafic) lava yields gentle flows.
Fissure eruptions (Basalt Plateau eruptions) formed the Deccan Traps in India, a favorite topic in Geography Prelims.
Differentiate between Vulcanian and Plinian types: Plinian eruptions produce sustained stratospheric ash columns and deadly pyroclastic density currents.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Hawaiian eruptions are the least explosive, featuring low-viscosity basaltic lava that flows smoothly over large distances.
Strombolian eruptions feature mild, frequent bursts of incandescent lava bombs and scoria, earning Mount Stromboli the moniker 'Lighthouse of the Mediterranean'.
Vulcanian eruptions are explosive releases of viscous magma that blow out hardened lava plugs, producing dark, ash-laden eruption clouds.
Pelean and Plinian eruptions represent the most violent eruption styles, characterized by pyroclastic flows and eruption columns reaching deep into the stratosphere.
The Volcanic Explosivity Index (VEI) measures the volume of pyroclastic material, cloud height, and explosion intensity on a logarithmic scale from 0 to 8.
